title: RTO2 Membership Projects Compute Candidates, Not Placement Rights
summary: Generalized Compute Intentions dev8 projects current RexxOS RTO2 MI membership into compute candidates while excluding MU control members and preserving exact member incarnation.
why: The estate already knows which MI objects currently exist. GCI should consume that object-rich membership evidence rather than maintain a second node catalogue, but membership must not become placement or lease authority.
invariants: MU members remain estate/control membership and are not projected as worker capacity.
MI members retain their native RTO2 member object and semantic reference inside the GCI resource wrapper.
An injected Grid eligibility policy decides whether the current MI incarnation is usable; GCI does not invent membership-state semantics.
The exact member ID and incarnation are rechecked before compute assessment.
Absent or reincarnated members fail closed as RTO2_MEMBER_ABSENT_OR_REINCARNATED.
RTO2 membership never grants WLU admission, Job-to-Node placement/lease, ACTIVE/SPARE or execution authority.
evidence_note: Grounded in GCI v0.1-dev8 GeneralizedComputeRTO2Adapter.cls and reviewed RexxOS RTO2 Grid v0.1-dev15 archive digest e94ba156182567752e7e3b86e88b6a0e8a25fb8710648bb373a4c33271226543.
